3_adapter_path.reason: Structurally impossible over this gold set; see limitations. Not attempted rather than approximated.

paired_significance_recall_at_10.test: exact two-sided McNemar over 35 paired queries
paired_significance_recall_at_10.power_note: With an exact two-sided sign test, p < 0.05 requires at least 6 discordant queries all in one direction. The largest observed discordance is 3. No direct-arm Recall@10 comparison on this 35-query corpus can reach conventional significance.

segment_count_drift_from_july.localisation: The entire structure-overlap delta is one artifact: congress-bill-v1 / 118-hr-8862, 64 segments then, 58 now. Its congress_bills.xml_text element stream went from 174 slices to 3,428.
segment_count_drift_from_july.attribution: e0af2b9 (2026-07-24 20:37) last changed src/spicy_regs/ontology/adapters.py; the baseline parquet was written 2026-07-24 18:11, 2.5 hours earlier. paragraph-sentence, which ignores the element stream, is unchanged at 1,276 — confirming the corpus is identical and the change is in element extraction.

decision.basis: Among the three lossless arms (35/35 gold contained) all tie at Recall@50 = 0.8000; the declared tiebreak is Recall@10, where structure-overlap leads 20/35 to 18/35 and never loses a query to structure-first. The lead is not statistically significant and cannot be made so on this corpus.

limitations: The sealed evaluation identity segmentation_eval_627ba96e04872d870a2ccd6e is permanently unreproducible on this machine. Every result here runs against a re-seal proven set-identical on artifacts, gold, and adversarial cases, but a reader who demands the original digest cannot get it.
The frozen parity gate fails and is left failing on purpose. Nothing in this receipt asserts that the committed segmenter reproduces the July baseline; it demonstrably does not.

The July fair comparison could not be re-run through the DocumentRelease adapter. The adapter mints a different artifact_digest space (sha256 of one representation's text) and a different source_field namespace, so no gold row's key survives the crossing; 152 of the 1,302 baseline segments span 2-6 source fields that a one-representation-per-artifact adapter cannot produce; no DocumentRelease exists over the 153 artifacts and no code builds one; and only structure-overlap is expressible through the production segmenter at all. Measuring the adapter's effect on this comparison was therefore not attempted rather than approximated.
OpenAI arms were not re-run: no paid provider calls were made. The July OpenAI-side result, including its structure-first advantage, is not re-verified here and this run says nothing about it.
The llm-guided arm uses the local heuristic boundary selector, matching the July BGE system-level row, not the OpenAI selector.
35 gold queries. Every metric difference reported is exact on this corpus and carries no confidence interval.
Reranking, sparse, hybrid, and whole-artifact stages of the July comparison were out of scope for this run.
